defs.def: a group into which animals, plants, etc. that are able to breed with each other and produce healthy young are divided, smaller than a genus and identified by a Latin name 种，物种（分类上小于属）

ex.s: The research, carried out by scientists at the Columbia Climate School and other institutions, found that if the city maintains past species patterns in new plantings, isoprene production in Manhattan in coming decades will go up by about 140%, and resulting summer ozone levels as much as 30%.
ex.t: 由哥伦比亚气候学院等机构的科学家进行的研究发现，如果该市在新种植中维持过去的物种格局，未来几十年曼哈顿的异戊二烯产量将上升约140%，由此导致的夏季臭氧水平将上升多达30%。

ex.s: “You have to think about what you would lose if you do that.” Oaks are keystone species, she pointed out, providing food and habitat for native insects, birds and other animals.
ex.t: “你得想想你那么做会失去什么。”她指出，橡树是关键物种，为本地的昆虫、鸟类和其他动物提供食物和栖息地。

ex.s: Changing the species of trees in new plantings.
ex.t: 改变新栽种中的树种.

ex.s: To bring in foreign species of plants.
ex.t: 以引进外来植物种.

ex.s: Being an adult is about having a rooted sense of self while being capable of identifying and managing your emotions and actions. ____38____ We are a social species, so this is important.
ex.t: 作为一个成年人,我们拥有一种根深蒂固的自我意识,同时能够识别和管理你的情感和行动。我____38____们是一个社会物种,所以这一点很重要。

ex.s: Habitat Restoration Team volunteers play a vital role in restoring sensitive resources and protecting endangered species across the ridges and valleys.
ex.t: 栖息地修复团队的志愿者在恢复敏感资源、保护山脊与山谷间的濒危物种方面发挥着重要作用。

ex.s: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records.
ex.t: 在物种灭绝前记录地球物种的竞赛中，研究人员和公民科学家已经收集了数十亿条记录。

ex.s: Though they are useful for detecting shifts in the number and variety of species in an area, a new Stanford study has found that this type of record is not perfect.
ex.t: 尽管它们有助于发现一个地区物种数量和种类的变化，斯坦福的一项新研究发现这类记录并不完美。

ex.s: “With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application,” said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences.
ex.t: 随着技术兴起，人们借助手机应用很容易观察不同物种，”该研究第一作者、斯坦福人文与科学学院生物学助理教授Barnabas Daru说。

ex.s: Moreover, these data are biased and favor certain regions, time periods, and species.
ex.t: 此外，这些数据存在偏差，偏向某些地区、时期和物种。

ex.s: This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby.
ex.t: 这说得通，因为在移动设备上获得观察性生物多样性数据的人，往往是记录附近物种遇见的公民科学家。

ex.s: These data are also biased toward certain species with attractive or eye-catching features.
ex.t: 这些数据也偏向某些具有吸引力或醒目特征的物种。

ex.s: “Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
ex.t: “生物多样性应用程序可以利用我们的研究结果，告知用户哪些地区采样过度，并把他们引导到采样不足的地方——甚至是不曾被充分采样的物种。”

ex.s: What do we know about the records of species collected now?
ex.t: 关于现在收集到的物种记录，我们知道什么？

ex.s: Further, the Silk Route Garden around the greenhouse ____60____ (walk) visitors through a journey influenced by the ancient Silk Road, by which silk as well as many plant species came to Britain for ____61____ first time.
ex.t: 此外,丝绸之路花园环绕着____60____温室游客,经过受古代丝绸之路影响的旅程,丝绸和许多植物物种首次____61____来到英国.

ex.s: The path offers over 300 plant species for visitors to see, too.
ex.t: 这条路也为游客提供了300多种植物。

ex.s: Our formative environment as a species was information-poor, so our brains developed a mechanism that prized new information.
ex.t: 作为人类，我们形成期的环境是信息匮乏的，因此我们的大脑形成了一种重视新信息的机制。

ex.s: While many species’ thought processes are limited to “Food, eat it!”, “Danger, run!”, “Pain, avoid!”, we’ve evolved beyond that.
ex.t: 虽然许多物种的思维仅限于“食物，吃它！”“危险，快跑！”“疼痛，避开！”，但我们已进化超越这些。

ex.s: According to the author, how are humans different from many other species?
ex.t: 根据作者的说法，人类与许多其他物种有何不同？

ex.s: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
ex.t: 1975年，灰熊被列入《濒危物种法》。

ex.s: Aloe vera, peace lilies and spider plants are some of the species that are easy to grow indoors.
ex.t: 芦荟、和平百合和吊兰是几种易于室内种植的植物。

ex.s: Human impact on the animal kingdom, such as hunting and destruction of habitats, ___________a reduction in the population of certain species in the past three decades.
ex.t: 人类对动物王国的影响，如狩猎和栖息地破坏，（第__空）过去三十年某些物种数量的减少。

ex.s: The GPNP is intended to provide stronger protection for all the species ____65____ live within the Giant Panda Range and significantly improve the health of the ecosystem in the area.
ex.t: 全球方案计划旨在为生活在大熊猫范围内的____65____所有物种提供更有力的保护,并显著改善该地区的生态系统健康。

ex.s: They are foreign species.
ex.t: 它们是外来物种。

ex.s: Indeed, it is thought that over four- fifths of living species on earth remain undiscovered.
ex.t: 确实，据认为地球上有超过五分之四的生物物种仍未被发现。

ex.s: Of course, if you are a non-human species, collapse is well underway.
ex.t: 当然，如果你是非人类物种，崩溃早已在进行中。

ex.s: Nutria are an endangered species.
ex.t: 海狸鼠是濒危物种。

ex.s: I began collecting newspaper articles about new species, new monkey, new spider…, and on and on they appear.
ex.t: 我开始收集关于新物种、新猴子、新蜘蛛……的报纸文章，它们源源不断地出现。

ex.s: I began a second drawer for more general discoveries: new cave system discovered with dozens of nameless species, four hundred species of bacteria found in the human stomach.
ex.t: 我为更一般的发现开了第二个抽屉：新发现的洞穴系统里有数十种无名物种，人体胃里发现了四百种细菌。

ex.s: The second drawer began to fill and as it did I wondered whether there were bigger discoveries out there, not just species, but life that depends on things thought to be useless, life even without DNA.
ex.t: 第二个抽屉开始被填满，随着它填满，我想知道外面是否有更大的发现，不只是物种，而是依赖被认为无用的东西的生命，甚至是没有DNA的生命。

ex.s: Mathematical models have also revealed that food webs may be unstable， where small changes of top predators can lead to big effects throughout entire ecosystems． In the 1960s， scientists proposed that predators at the top of a food web had a surprising amount of control over the size of populations of other species﹣including species they did not directly attack．
ex.t: 数学模型也揭示，食物网可能不稳定，顶级捕食者的微小变化会在整个生态系统引发巨大效应。20世纪60年代，科学家提出，食物网顶端的捕食者对包括它们不直接攻击的物种在内的其他物种种群规模有着惊人的控制力。

ex.t: A．食物网中物种的生活习性。

ex.s: C．The approaches to studying die species in the ecosystems．
ex.t: C．研究生态系统中该物种的方法。

ex.s: British_______Charles Darwin(1809-1882) is best known for his work On the Origin of species, in which he explains changes in species due to natural selection.
ex.t: 英属夏尔·达尔文(1809年-1882年)以其作品"物种起源"最为著名,其中他解释了由于自然选择而导致的物种变化.

ex.s: As he studied these, he asked himself the question: how did different species come to exist?
ex.t: 当他研究这些东西时,他自问一个问题:不同的物种是如何存在的?

ex.s: He noticed that some species of animals were very similar to each other.
ex.t: 他注意到一些动物种类彼此非常相似.

ex.s: Over time, it had slowly evolved into many new species.
ex.t: 随着时间的推移,它慢慢地演变成许多新物种.
